title: Methods for Dynamic Re-Focussing of an Electron Energy-Loss Spectrum
content: Since long electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) is routinely used to collect low-loss and core-loss analytical signals. Fast methods to shift the spectral region of interest along the energy axis have been successfully combined with multiple-exposure techniques [1, 2]. This allows to extent the accessible energy range for STEM spectrum imaging and to compensate for the limited dynamical range of most electron detectors. While modern spectrometers with low-dispersion settings in combination with hybrid-pixel detectors with large dynamic range allow to capture a wide spectral range of several keV with only one exposure [3, 4], dual- or multiple-range EELS techniques are still very useful to simultaneouly collect information from several energy-loss regions with high dispersion and sufficient energy resolution [5].
